subject: [RFC PATCH 0/4] mm/zswap: make shrinker writeback work with iocost

reviews.author: Christoph Hellwig
reviews.summary: Raised concerns about the implications of using REQ_BACKGROUND for throttled I/O. Suggested that the caller should be able to tolerate a failure, implying that foreground paging is not suitable.
reviews.raw_body:
On Mon, Sep 28, 2026 at 10:18:36AM +0200, Alexandre Ghiti wrote:
> bio_issue_as_root_blkg() issues every REQ_SWAP bio as root, bypassing
> the cgroup IO controllers, because reclaim cannot stall indefinitely on
> swap writes. Some swap writes are not urgent though: zswap writeback is
> best effort.
> 
> Such a bio cannot simply drop REQ_SWAP: dm-crypt and dm-thin rely on it
> for limit_swap_bios, which caps in-flight swap bios to avoid a memory
> deadlock, see commit a666e5c05e7c ("dm: fix deadlock when swapping to
> encrypted device").

Is that true?  REQ_BACKGROUND very much implies the I/O can the throttled
and thus better not be foreground paging, and thus the caller should be
able to tolerate a failure.

2026-09-28.patch_summary: This RFC patch series aims to improve the performance of zswap by making its shrinker writeback work with iocost. The current implementation causes a large production workload to be slower when zswap is enabled, due to two main issues: (1) zswap writeback being charged as debt and causing stalls in application allocations, and (2) throttled writes sleeping in their submitter, which can be an application thread. The patches propose to throttle zswap writeback instead of making it REQ_SWAP, and move the reclaim-driven writeback to a per-lruvec kworker.
